newsitem.title: INDIA: TELCO tops Templeton India's portfolio.
newsitem.headline: TELCO tops Templeton India's portfolio.

text.p: Templeton Asset Management India Ltd said shares of India's leading truck maker Tata Engineering and Locomotive Company Ltd (TELCO) topped the portfolio of its maiden Indian fund Templeton India Growth Fund.
Templeton said it held 170,000 shares of TELCO valued at 76.84 million rupees as of June 30, 1997.
India's state-run refiner Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) ranked second in the portfolio, accounting for 60.70 million rupees.

Engineering and construction firm Larsen & Toubro, cement maker Gujarat Ambuja Cements and telephone firm Mahanagar Telephone Nigam Ltd ranked third, fourth and fifth in Templeton's holdings, the company said in a note to unit holders.
The market value of Templeton India Growth Fund's total share holdings amounted to 783.40 million rupees as on June 30.
Investment in cash and cash equivalent amounted to 281.52 million rupees. The net asset value of the fund as on June 30 was 11.83 rupees, the company said.

In a communication to unit holders, J. Mark Mobius, director, Templeton Asset Management (India), said he welcomed the Reserve Bank of India committee's report recommending a phased movement towards capital convertibility of the rupee beginning 1997/98 (April-March).

"While liberalisation is always welcome, much more needs to be done to improve the process of investing in India and to remove the remaining restrictions on capital movement into and out of the country," the communication said.
"However, we are broadly pleased with the progress that has been made so far and continue to see good prospects for the market and the fund."
